title: CPSC, Madrigal Announce Recall of Subwoofers
reason: A screw inside of the subwoofer can cause a high voltage short, which could cause a severe injury to consumers, through an electric shock.
firm: Madrigal Audio Laboratories, Inc., of Middletown, Conn.
distribution: Specialty audio dealers sold the subwoofers nationwide and in Puerto Rico, from January 2001 through October 2002, for about $3,000.
hazards: A screw inside of the subwoofer can cause a high voltage short, which could cause a severe injury to consumers, through an electric shock.
remedies: Consumers should not touch the rear panel, use the power switch, or remove the power cord or any connections from the back of the unit until it is repaired.
injuries: Madrigal has received one report of electric shock; though, no injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Wooden Toy Vehicles
reason: These products may be given to children as toys. The wheels on the wooden toys may break off into small parts, which may pose a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Kmart stores nationwide sold these wooden vehicles, from November 2002 through December 2002, for about $5.
hazards: These products may be given to children as toys. The wheels on the wooden toys may break off into small parts, which may pose a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take them away from children immediately and return them to any Kmart store for a full refund.
injuries: Kmart has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Century Tool and Manufacturing Announce Recall of Camping Stoves
reason: The burner assembly in the stoves can restrict the flow of gas, which can cause a leak. The leaking gas can ignite and weaken the hose, causing it to separate from the stove and pose a fire hazard to consumers.
firm: Century Tool and Manufacturing Co. Inc., of Cherry Valley, Ill.
distribution: Sporting goods, camping supply and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold these stoves, from May 2002 through September 2002, for up to $90.
hazards: The burner assembly in the stoves can restrict the flow of gas, which can cause a leak. The leaking gas can ignite and weaken the hose, causing it to separate from the stove and pose a fire hazard to consumers.
remedies: The firm that announced the recall is no longer in business. Consumers should stop using the product immediately and contact the previous owner to arrange for returning the product and receiving a refund.
injuries: Century Tool and Manufacturing has received eight reports of hoses separating from the stove, causing one minor injury.

title: CPSC, Brooklyn Lollipop Announce Recall of Electric Fans
reason: These electric fans have undersized wiring, use a power plug that is not polarized, have an improperly sized grill, and overheat, all of which could cause electrocution, electric shock, fire, and finger entrapment hazards to consumers.
distribution: Discount and variety stores in the metropolitan New York area sold these electric fans, from May 2000 through July 2002, for between $10 and $15.
hazards: These electric fans have undersized wiring, use a power plug that is not polarized, have an improperly sized grill, and overheat, all of which could cause electrocution, electric shock, fire, and finger entrapment hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these electric fans immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund. Consumers also can return the fans to the firm for a full refund, by mailing the unit to: 7 Marcus Garvey Blvd., Brooklyn, NY 11206.
injuries: CPSC and Brooklyn Lollipop have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Atico International Announce Recall of Christmas Candles
reason: The wick is not properly set inside the tealight, which may cause the plastic holder to melt and pose a fire hazard to consumers.
distribution: Eckerds, Kerr Drugs, Snyders Drugstore, and Farmacias El Amal stores nationwide sold the candles, from September 2002 through December 2002, for between $2.50 and $4.
hazards: The wick is not properly set inside the tealight, which may cause the plastic holder to melt and pose a fire hazard to consumers.
remedies: The firm is out of business, the remedy is no longer available, and the product should be discarded or destroyed.
injuries: Atico has received one report involving melting of the plastic holder; however, no injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Lovee Doll & Toy Co., Inc. Announce Recall of Talking Dolls
reason: Buttons on the dolls' outfit could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Toy and discount department stores sold the dolls nationwide, from June 2002 through December 2002, for between $10 and $15.
hazards: Buttons on the dolls' outfit could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these dolls away from children immediately and return the dolls to the store where it was purchased for a refund.
injuries: Lovee Doll and Toy Co., Inc. has not received any reports of incidents involving these dolls. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Kohl's Department Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Fleece Pant Sets
reason: Small pieces of fabric at the end of the sleeves, along the hem and on the pockets of the tops can be torn off easily, posing a choking hazard.
distribution: Kohl's Department Stores sold the pant set nationwide, from September 2002 through early November 2002, for about $18.
hazards: Small pieces of fabric at the end of the sleeves, along the hem and on the pockets of the tops can be torn off easily, posing a choking hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the set immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a refund.
injuries: Kohl's Department Stores Inc. has received two reports of young children putting torn pieces of fabric in their mouths. One child reportedly began to choke on a piece of material.

title: CPSC, Elkton Sparkler Announce Recall of Bamboo-Stick Sparklers
reason: The sparklers' bamboo-stick handles can catch fire, burn and disintegrate and emit burning fragments during use. The sparklers present a fire hazard and a risk of burn injury.
distribution: Variety Stores sold these sparklers nationwide, from January 2002 through May 2002, for between $2 and $5 a box.
hazards: The sparklers' bamboo-stick handles can catch fire, burn and disintegrate and emit burning fragments during use. The sparklers present a fire hazard and a risk of burn injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these sparklers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Elkton Sparkler have received four reports of burns and clothing igniting. Injuries include a 6-year-old girl, who received second-degree burns to her ankle, and a 3-year-old boy, who received a minor burn to his leg when his sweat pants caught on fire.

title: CPSC, Zutano Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Bunny Toys
reason: The buttons on the front of the bunny's jacket can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold the recalled bunny toys, from July 2000 through December 2002, for about $18.
hazards: The buttons on the front of the bunny's jacket can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these recalled bunny toys away from young children immediately and contact Zutano Inc. to receive a replacement outfit.
injuries: Zutano has not received any reports of injuries relating to these stuffed bunny toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Wear Me Apparel Corp. Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garments
reason: The paint on the "smiley face" zipper-pull attached to the sweat jacket of these garments contains lead. Young children could ingest lead from the zipper-pull, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.
distribution: Kmart stores nationwide exclusively sold these garments, from August 2002 through October 2002, for between $10 and $13.
hazards: The paint on the "smiley face" zipper-pull attached to the sweat jacket of these garments contains lead. Young children could ingest lead from the zipper-pull, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.
remedies: Consumers should return the clothing sets to any Kmart store to receive a full refund.
injuries: Wear Me Apparel Corp. and CPSC have not received any reports of injuries involving these garments. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® Announce Recall of Motion Lamps
reason: Wires near the light's socket can become exposed, posing a risk of electric shock or electrocution to consumers.
distribution: Cracker Barrel Old Country Stores® sold the motion lamps nationwide, from August 2002 through October 2002, for about $20.
hazards: Wires near the light's socket can become exposed, posing a risk of electric shock or electrocution to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using and unplug these lamps immediately and contact Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® to receive a full refund.
injuries: There have been no reports of incidents or injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Philips Announce Recall 3-in-1 Waffle Maker/Sandwich Maker/Grill
reason: The hinges of the sandwich plate can contact an internal wire, creating a risk of shock or electrocution.
distribution: Target Stores sold this product, from September 2002 to October 2002, for about $50.
hazards: The hinges of the sandwich plate can contact an internal wire, creating a risk of shock or electrocution.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled 3-in-1 Waffle Maker/Sandwich Maker/Grill immediately, unplug it, and return the product to Target Stores for a full refund.
injuries: There has been one report overseas of the sandwich plate contacting an internal wire, which did not result in a shock or injury. No incidents or injuries have been reported in the United States.

title: CPSC, Montrose Wholesale Candies & Sundries Inc. Announce Recall of Illegally Imported Cigarette Lighters
reason: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
distribution: Convenience, gas, and grocery stores in the central U.S. sold these disposable cigarette lighters, from September 2002 through December 2002, for about $1.
hazards: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Montrose Wholesale Candies and Sundries are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Milwaukee Tool Corp. Announce Recall of Electric Grinders
reason: The grinder's switch can stick in the "on" position, which could pose an injury hazard to consumers.
firm: Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp., of Brookfield, Wis.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial distributors nationwide sold these grinders, from June 2001 through November 2002, for between $165 and $175.
hazards: The grinder's switch can stick in the "on" position, which could pose an injury hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the grinders immediately and return them to their nearest Milwaukee factory service center or authorized power tool service center, for a free repair.
injuries: CPSC and Milwaukee Electric Tool have received 12 reports of grinder switches sticking in the "on" position; however, no injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Makita U.S.A. Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Circular Saws
reason: The lower blade guard of the saw can become jammed, which can result in the consumer coming in contact with the blade and suffering a serious injury.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial suppliers nationwide sold the circular saws, from April 1998 to November 2002, for between $99 and $119.
hazards: The lower blade guard of the saw can become jammed, which can result in the consumer coming in contact with the blade and suffering a serious injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the circular saws immediately and return them to the nearest Makita factory service center for a free repair.
injuries: Makita U.S.A. Inc. has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, The Lakeside Collection Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
product: Kid's Tent Set (only the tunnel is recalled)
reason: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
distribution: The tent sets were sold by The Lakeside Collection, from May 2002 through November 2002, for about $23.
hazards: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact The Lakeside Collection to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by The Lakeside Collection.
injuries: There have been no injuries.

title: CPSC, Home Interiors and Gifts Announce Recall of Tea Lights
reason: Flames from the tea lights can flare, and the excessive heat can cause the plastic holders to melt, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Home Interiors' direct sales associates exclusively sold the recalled tea lights, from September 2002 through November 2002, for about $5 per box.
hazards: Flames from the tea lights can flare, and the excessive heat can cause the plastic holders to melt, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the tea lights immediately and return any unused tea lights by mail to Home Interiors at 2901 Trade Center Drive, Suite 100, Carrollton, TX 75007. Consumers should include their return address information to receive a retail gift certificate from Home Interiors, for the full purchase cost and shipping cost of the tea lights.
injuries: Home Interiors and Gifts has received 22 reports of the tea lights flaring up and melting their plastic holders. These incidents have resulted in minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC and S.I.T. Announce Recall of Plastic Stack Chairs
reason: The chairs can collapse during use, causing the consumer to suffer injuries from falls.
distribution: Drug stores sold the plastic stack chairs nationwide, from April 2000 through September 2002, for between $4 and $6.
hazards: The chairs can collapse during use, causing the consumer to suffer injuries from falls.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these plastic chairs immediately and contact S.I.T. to receive a refund.
injuries: S.I.T. has received two reports of the chairs collapsing. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Oceanic USA Announce Recall of Scuba Regulators
reason: Extreme vibration can occur within these CDX regulators, which can cause an air leakage underwater. Divers could run out of air and drown.
firm: Oceanic USA, of San Leandro, Calif.
distribution: Authorized Oceanic dealers sold these regulator sets worldwide, from May 1999 through October 2002, for between $330 to $640, depending on the second stage.
hazards: Extreme vibration can occur within these CDX regulators, which can cause an air leakage underwater. Divers could run out of air and drown.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled CDX regulators immediately and take them to any authorized Oceanic dealer to get a free repair. Other repairs or normal maintenance performed in addition to the recall repair will incur a charge.
injuries: Oceanic has received six reports of noise or vibration accompanied by air leakage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, LTD Commodities, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
reason: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
distribution: The tent sets were sold by LTD Commodities, Inc., from May 2002 through November 2002, for about $23.
hazards: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact LTD Commodities, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by LTD Commodities, Inc.
injuries: LTD Commodities, Inc received one report, in which a child's leg was cut, requiring nine stitches.

title: CPSC, Tecumseh Products Co. Announce Recall of Power Equipment Engines
reason: A misrouted fuel line in the engine can become damaged, allowing gasoline to leak out, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
firm: Tecumseh Products Co., Tecumseh, Mich.
distribution: Products equipped with the recalled engines were sold by retailers and dealers nationwide, from June 2002 through November 2002. Sears, Roebuck & Co. distributed a limited quantity of these recalled products under its Craftsman brand name.
hazards: A misrouted fuel line in the engine can become damaged, allowing gasoline to leak out, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the power equipment immediately and contact Tecumseh to schedule a free engine repair.
injuries: Tecumseh has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Good Lad Apparel Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garment and Shoes
reason: Small decorative items on the garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Department stores sold the infant garments nationwide, from January 2002 through April 2002, for about $15.
hazards: Small decorative items on the garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these garments and sandals immediately. Consumers should return the garments to the store where purchased to receive a refund.
injuries: Good Lad has received three reports of incidents involving the decorative items. A child swallowed a decorative ladybug and two others began to choke on decorative flowers. There have been no reports of injury.

title: CPSC, Honda Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)
reason: Vehicle Accident
firm: American Honda Motor Co. Inc., of Torrance Calif.
distribution: Honda motorcycle dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from July 2002 through October 2002, for approximately $7,000.
hazards: Vehicle Accident
remedies: Consumers should stop using these ATVs immediately and call their local Honda ATV dealer to schedule a free repair. Consumers should not attempt to torque these bolts themselves because this job requires shop equipment and special tools not generally available to consumers. Registered owners of the vehicles have been notified directly by American Honda.
injuries: Honda has received one report of a bolt falling out and a front suspension collapsing on one of these vehicles. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Cannondale Corp. Announce Recall of ATVs
reason: The front shocks can break apart internally while riding. If this happens, the shock halves can separate, causing the ATV suspension to fail. The operator can lose control of the ATV, possibly resulting in injury or death.
firm: Cannondale Corp., of Bethel, Conn.
distribution: Cannondale dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from February 2002 through September 2002, for $7,000.
hazards: The front shocks can break apart internally while riding. If this happens, the shock halves can separate, causing the ATV suspension to fail. The operator can lose control of the ATV, possibly resulting in injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should stop riding these ATVs and contact their local Cannondale dealer to schedule an appointment to have the front shocks replaced for free.
injuries: Cannondale Corp. has received 11 reports of these front shocks breaking apart. One consumer has suffered a broken leg.

title: CPSC, abc Distributing, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
reason: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible laceration injuries.
distribution: The tent sets were sold by abc Distributing, Inc., from March 2002 through June 2002, for about $23.
hazards: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible laceration injuries.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact abc Distributing, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement, at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by abc Distributing, Inc.
injuries: abc Distributing, Inc. has received three reports, two with minor injuries, as a result of the tip of the wire becoming exposed.

title: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of Toy Attachments on Baby Walkers
reason: The flower toys on the baby walker's tray can detach from the stems, exposing sharp edges and posing a laceration hazard to young children.
distribution: Discount, department and juvenile product stores sold the walkers with these toys nationwide, from December 2000 through October 2002, for between $20 and $40.
hazards: The flower toys on the baby walker's tray can detach from the stems, exposing sharp edges and posing a laceration hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should remove the detachable toy bars or music center toy trays on these walkers immediately.
injuries: Kolcraft has received 15 reports of injuries associated with the exposed sharp edges of the toys' stems. The injuries to children included lacerations around the eyes, eyelids, face and tongue.

title: CPSC, Disney Store Announce Recall of Monsters, Inc. Character Plush Dolls
reason: The Boo doll's hair has ponytail holders that could detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.
distribution: The Disney Stores nationwide exclusively sold these plush dolls, from July 2002 through October 2002, for about $20.
hazards: The Boo doll's hair has ponytail holders that could detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the two pink ponytail holders and two rubber bands from the Boo doll's hair or return the item to any Disney Store for a full refund.
injuries: The Disney Store has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these dolls and is voluntarily recalling them to prevent future incidents.

title: CPSC, Baby Trend Announce Recall to Repair Infant Swings Sold at Toys R Us
reason: A screw on the swing's support arm can loosen or detach, causing the seat to separate and drop to one side. This presents a fall hazard to infants.
distribution: Toys R Us stores sold these swings nationwide, from November 2001 through September 2002, for between $60 and $90.
hazards: A screw on the swing's support arm can loosen or detach, causing the seat to separate and drop to one side. This presents a fall hazard to infants.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these recalled swings immediately and contact Baby Trend to receive a free repair kit.
injuries: Baby Trend has received 10 reports of the screws loosening. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Meijer Announce Recall of Three-Tier Tealight Candleholder
reason: The middle candleholder is mounted directly below the top candleholder, which can cause the top candle to overheat and flare. This poses a fire hazard, which can result in a burn injury or property damage.
distribution: Meijer stores located in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois sold the candleholders, from May 2002 through October 2002, for about $7.99.
hazards: The middle candleholder is mounted directly below the top candleholder, which can cause the top candle to overheat and flare. This poses a fire hazard, which can result in a burn injury or property damage.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the candleholder immediately and return it to their local Meijer store for a refund.
injuries: There have been two incidents of candles flaring. The incidents did not result in injury or property damage. Meijer is recalling the candleholder to prevent injury or property damage.

title: CPSC, Target Corp. Announce Recall of Men's Sweatshirts
reason: The fleece fabric on the inside of these sweatshirts fails to meet federal mandatory standards of fabric flammability, because it can ignite readily if exposed to flame, and therefore presents a serious risk of burn injuries, in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
firm: Trends Clothing Corp., of Miami, Fla.
distribution: Target Stores nationwide sold the sweatshirts, from August 2002 through September 2002, for about $25.
hazards: The fleece fabric on the inside of these sweatshirts fails to meet federal mandatory standards of fabric flammability, because it can ignite readily if exposed to flame, and therefore presents a serious risk of burn injuries, in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop wearing these sweatshirts and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Target are not aware of any injuries involving these sweatshirts. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Evercel Announce Recall of Nickel Zinc Battery Chargers
reason: Internal electrical components of the battery chargers can overheat, posing a fire hazard.
firm: Evercel Inc., of Hingham, Mass.
distribution: Cabella's mail order catalogs and web site sold these battery chargers as part of their Evercel Model MOD100-7C Trolling Battery system, from August 2002 through September 2002, for about $299.
hazards: Internal electrical components of the battery chargers can overheat, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these battery chargers immediately and discard them in accordance with local laws.
injuries: There have been three reports of these battery chargers overheating and melting, causing minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Estyle, Inc. recall Children's Jackets
reason: The jackets do not meet the Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles under the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
firm: Estyle, Inc. of Los Angeles, Calif.
distribution: Estyle sold the jackets on their web site, from March 2002 through June 2002, for about $68.
hazards: The jackets do not meet the Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles under the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the jackets immediately and contact Estyle, Inc. for a full refund.

title: CPSC, Bear Archery LLC Announce Recall of Compound Bows
reason: The limbs of these bows can break during use, causing impact injuries to consumers.
distribution: Hunting & sporting goods stores, mass merchants and catalogs nationwide sold the bows, from September 2002 through October 2002, for between $75 and $100.
hazards: The limbs of these bows can break during use, causing impact injuries to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled bows immediately and contact Bear Archery for a free replacement.
injuries: Bear Archery has received about 200 reports of these bows breaking during use, with reports of seven minor injuries, such as cuts and bruises to the face and chest.

title: CPSC, Halo Burger Announce Recall of Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals
product: Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals
reason: The "AA" batteries provided with each flashlight can leak, which could cause irritation to the skin. When disassembled, the flashlights also have small parts that can pose a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Halo Burger restaurants distributed the flashlights as a premium with the kids meals in Genesee and Saginaw Counties in Michigan, from October 2002 through November 4, 2002. The flashlights were sold individually for about $1.50.
hazards: The "AA" batteries provided with each flashlight can leak, which could cause irritation to the skin. When disassembled, the flashlights also have small parts that can pose a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these flashlights and batteries away from children immediately and return the flashlights and batteries to any Halo Burger restaurant to receive a $5 gift certificate, or discard flashlights and batteries in a safe manner.
injuries: Halo Burger received two reports of young children, who received minor skin irritation on their mouths from leaking flashlight batteries.

title: CPSC, Stihl Inc. Announce Recall of Chain Saws
reason: Fuel can leak out of the chain saw's tank, which could cause a fire or injury hazard to consumers.
firm: Stihl Inc., of Virginia Beach, Va.
distribution: Stihl dealers nationwide sold the chain saws, from July 2002 through October 2002, for between $180 and $200.
hazards: Fuel can leak out of the chain saw's tank, which could cause a fire or injury hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the chain saws immediately and return them to the dealer where purchased, for a free repair.
injuries: Stihl has received six reports of fuel leakage. No fires or injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Miracle Recreation Equipment Company Announce Recall of Public Playground Equipment Swing Seats
reason: Metal inserts inside the swing seats can wear through and cause lacerations to children.
firm: Miracle Recreation Equipment Company, of Monett, Mo.
distribution: Miracle Recreation Equipment Company sold the swing seats nationwide, from June 2001 to September 2002, for use on public playground equipment.
hazards: Metal inserts inside the swing seats can wear through and cause lacerations to children.
remedies: Owners should immediately stop children from using these swing seats and contact Miracle Recreation Co. for free replacement seats and hardware. If there are already exposed metal inserts on the edges of your seats, immediately take down the seats and chains. Do not leave chains on equipment, as children could seriously injure themselves or others with free-hanging chains. Purchasers were previously sent direct mail notification about this recall.
injuries: Two children have been injured and received stitches to lacerations on an arm and a leg, from exposed metal on edges of swing seats.

title: CPSC, Eveready Battery Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Kidz Club Flashlights
reason: The flashlights can overheat and cause the batteries to leak, posing a risk of burns to children.
distribution: Discount department and toy stores sold these flashlights nationwide, from April 2002 through October 2002, for about $6.
hazards: The flashlights can overheat and cause the batteries to leak, posing a risk of burns to children.
remedies: Consumers should take these flashlights away from children immediately and remove the batteries and contact Eveready for instructions on returning the flashlights and receiving a $12 refund.
injuries: Eveready has received three reports of the flashlights overheating, including one report of a 4-year-old boy receiving a minor burn to his hand.

title: CPSC, Damo Plus Corp. Announce Recall of Children's School Supply Sets
reason: The sets contain razor knives, which pose a laceration hazard to children.
distribution: Discount and dollar stores in California, Texas, Washington, and Maryland sold the sets, between June and October 2002, for about $1.
hazards: The sets contain razor knives, which pose a laceration hazard to children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take these razor knives away from children and return the pencil sets to the store where they purchased them, for a refund.
injuries: Damo Plus has not received any reports of injuries from these pencil sets.

title: CPSC, Gen-X Sports Incorporated Announce Recall of Skateboard Ramp
reason: The ramps can crack, causing users to fall and suffer injuries.
distribution: Discount department and sports stores sold the ramps nationwide, from March 2002 through September 2002, for between $20 and $40.
hazards: The ramps can crack, causing users to fall and suffer injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these ramps immediately and contact Gen-X to receive a refund.
injuries: Gen-X Sports has received one report of the ramp cracking. The user, who was riding a scooter at the time of the incident, fell and broke his collarbone.

title: CPSC, Sunrise Medical Announce Recall of 3-Wheel Hand Cycle
reason: There is a small risk that the quick release axles of the rear wheels do not lock correctly. If the quick release axle is not fully and properly engaged, the wheel could become detached while moving. A detached wheel could result in loss of control of the cycle and potential for serious injury or death, due to a fall or collision with another object.
firm: Sunrise Medical of Heidelberg, Germany
distribution: Sunrise Medical dealers nationwide sold these hand cycles, from August 2001 to July 2002, for $3,300.
hazards: There is a small risk that the quick release axles of the rear wheels do not lock correctly. If the quick release axle is not fully and properly engaged, the wheel could become detached while moving. A detached wheel could result in loss of control of the cycle and potential for serious injury or death, due to a fall or collision with another object.
remedies: Consumers should stop riding these cycles immediately and contact their local Sunrise Medical dealer for a free repair.
injuries: Sunrise Medical has received one report, in which the quick release failed and the rider suffered minor injuries.

title: CPSC, Kohl's Department Stores Announce Recall of Halloween Candleholders
reason: Flames from the tea-light candle can ignite the candleholder, posing a fire hazard and risk of burn injuries to consumers.
distribution: Kohl's Department Stores sold the candleholders nationwide, from August 2002 through October 2002, for about $17.
hazards: Flames from the tea-light candle can ignite the candleholder, posing a fire hazard and risk of burn injuries to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the candleholders immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.

title: CPSC, LPK International Announce Recall of Barstools

injuries: Answer Products has received 18 reports of these adjusters separating from the fork and being projected at riders, causing four consumers to suffer cuts, bruises and one chipped tooth.

title: CPSC, Polaris Industries Inc. Announce Recall of RANGER Off-Road Utility Vehicles and Professional Series Utility Task Vehicles ("UTVs")
product: RANGER Off-Road Utility Vehicles and Professional Series Utility Task Vehicles (UTVs)
reason: The problem with the RANGER vehicles and UTVs involves the swing arm, which is part of the rear suspension. During operation of the vehicle, the pivot bolts of the swing arm can loosen and fall out. If this happens, the swing arm can become partially disconnected from the frame. This can result in the vehicle losing power, because the drivetrain connection to the wheels is no longer maintained. If this were to occur, the loss of power and resulting swing arm disorientation could cause the operator to lose control of the vehicle, resulting in injury to the operator.
firm: Polaris Industries Inc., of Minneapolis, Minn.
distribution: Polaris dealers sold these vehicles worldwide, from April 2001 through July 2002, for between $6,999 (2x4 model) to $9,949 (6x6 model) depending on the particular model.
hazards: The problem with the RANGER vehicles and UTVs involves the swing arm, which is part of the rear suspension. During operation of the vehicle, the pivot bolts of the swing arm can loosen and fall out. If this happens, the swing arm can become partially disconnected from the frame. This can result in the vehicle losing power, because the drivetrain connection to the wheels is no longer maintained. If this were to occur, the loss of power and resulting swing arm disorientation could cause the operator to lose control of the vehicle, resulting in injury to the operator.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these vehicles immediately and contact their local Polaris dealer to schedule an appointment for a free repair.
injuries: Polaris Industries Inc. has received twenty-three reports possibly related to the loose pivot bolt issue. One passenger was injured when she bumped her head on the cab frame.

title: CPSC, Arctic Cat Inc. Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles

title: CPSC and Shindaiwa Announce Recall of Hedge Trimmers Sold in California

title: CPSC, MTD Products Inc. Announce Recall of Grass Bags Used On Electric Lawn Mowers

title: CPSC, Electrolux Home Products, Inc. Announce Recall of Garden Tractors

This information is located under the tractor seat on the fender. We will verify if your tractor is affected by this recall. If your tractor is affected, we will schedule a free repair of the unit.

title: CPSC, Wal-Mart Announce Recall of Red Devil Gas Grills Sold at Wal-Mart
reason: The product's design allows consumers to light the grill at an air intake tube, instead of at the burner. Though the grill appears to function normally, gas inside the air intake tube ignites. The tube can reach temperatures of up to 750 degrees Fahrenheit and present a burn hazard to consumers. In some earlier grills, the heat produced by lighting the grill at the air intake tube damaged the plastic support piece and caused the grill to fall to the ground. When it collapses, flames from the grill can burn nearby consumers and ignite surrounding combustibles.
firm: Quantum North America Inc., of Encino, Calif.; e4L Inc., of Encino, Calif.
distribution: Quantum and e4L sold these grills directly to consumers through television infomercials, from about May 1998 through January 1999, for about $160. This recall only includes grills sold at Wal-Mart.
hazards: The product's design allows consumers to light the grill at an air intake tube, instead of at the burner. Though the grill appears to function normally, gas inside the air intake tube ignites. The tube can reach temperatures of up to 750 degrees Fahrenheit and present a burn hazard to consumers. In some earlier grills, the heat produced by lighting the grill at the air intake tube damaged the plastic support piece and caused the grill to fall to the ground. When it collapses, flames from the grill can burn nearby consumers and ignite surrounding combustibles.
remedies: CPSC urges consumers to stop using these grills immediately. Consumers who purchased Red Devil gas grills from Wal-Mart can return them to the store for a refund. Consumers who purchased their Red Devil Gas Grills from a retailer other than Wal-Mart should contact the retailer. If that retailer does not provide a refund, repair or replacement for the grill, consumers should contact CPSC. Additionally, consumers who are aware of any incidents with these grills or who want additional information also should contact CPSC.
injuries: There have been 44 reports of consumers suffering burns to legs, hands and fingers, including reports of some third degree burns, after the grills collapsed during use. More than 1,000 consumers returned their grills to the manufacturer because the grills collapsed. There have been no reports of incidents or injuries involving these grills sold by Wal-Mart.

injuries: Flat Rock Grill Co. had received six reports of the glass casing of the thermometers on these grills breaking. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC Issues Warning About Hazardous Red Devil Gas Grills
reason: The product's design allows consumers to light the grill at an air intake tube, instead of at the burner. Though the grill appears to function normally, gas inside the air intake tube ignites. The tube can reach temperatures of up to 750 degrees Fahrenheit and present a burn hazard to consumers. In some earlier grills, the heat produced by lighting the grill at the air intake tube damaged the plastic support piece, and caused the grill to fall to the ground. When it collapses, flames from the grill can burn nearby consumers and ignite surrounding combustibles.
firm: Quantum North America Inc., of Encino, Calif.; e4L Inc., of Encino, Calif.
distribution: Quantum and e4L sold these grills directly to consumers through television infomercials, from about May 1998 through January 1999, for about $160.
hazards: The product's design allows consumers to light the grill at an air intake tube, instead of at the burner. Though the grill appears to function normally, gas inside the air intake tube ignites. The tube can reach temperatures of up to 750 degrees Fahrenheit and present a burn hazard to consumers. In some earlier grills, the heat produced by lighting the grill at the air intake tube damaged the plastic support piece, and caused the grill to fall to the ground. When it collapses, flames from the grill can burn nearby consumers and ignite surrounding combustibles.
remedies: Both the Home Shopping Network (HSN) and QVC voluntarily notified their customers directly about the hazard these grills pose, and provided a remedy. Grills purchased from retailers other than the HSN and QVC are dangerous, and CPSC urges consumers to stop using them immediately. Since Quantum and e4l have declared bankruptcy, there is no remedy available. Vendors who are still selling these grills also are encouraged to stop doing so and contact CPSC. About 19,300 of these grills, sold directly by e4L, were recalled in July 1998 because the burners could disconnect from the burner pan. Even if consumers participated in this previous recall program, they should stop using these grills since this warning addresses a different hazard.
injuries: The firm received 21 reports of the burners on these grills disconnecting and one consumer suffered burns. There have been 44 reports of consumers suffering burns to legs, hands and fingers, including reports of some third degree burns, after the grills collapsed during use. More than 1,000 consumers returned their grills to the manufacturers because the grills collapsed.

title: CPSC and Sears Announce Recall of Riding Lawn Mower
reason: Under certain operating conditions, the vehicle's transmission may fail, causing a loss of drive and brake ability. Should this occur, the potential for personal injury and/or property damage exists.
distribution: Sears sold these riding lawn mowers nationwide, from February 2002 to April 2002, for about $999.
hazards: Under certain operating conditions, the vehicle's transmission may fail, causing a loss of drive and brake ability. Should this occur, the potential for personal injury and/or property damage exists.
remedies: Consumers should stop using their riding lawn mowers immediately and contact Sears to schedule an appointment to have a free new transmission installed. Purchasers were notified by direct mail notification.

title: CPSC, Best Lock Corp. Announce Recall of Electronic Door Locks
reason: In an extreme fire situation, it is possible for the electronic wires and mounting holes to become exposed, posing a fire hazard risk. There is no danger of latch failure, nor will this prevent normal egress during an emergency evacuation.
firm: Best Lock Corp., d/b/a/ Best Access Systems, of Indianapolis, Ind.
distribution: The IDH Max™, B.A.S.I.S.® G and B.A.S.I.S.® V products were sold directly or through authorized distributors to the commercial and industrial markets, between 2000 and December 2001.
hazards: In an extreme fire situation, it is possible for the electronic wires and mounting holes to become exposed, posing a fire hazard risk. There is no danger of latch failure, nor will this prevent normal egress during an emergency evacuation.
remedies: Customers will be contacted directly by Best Access Systems to receive a replacement product. Products installed in non-fire rated applications and B.A.S.I.S. G mortise products installed in 20-minute fire rated applications will be modified or replaced if requested by the customer. Products installed in 3-hour fire rated applications will be modified or replaced.
injuries: CPSC and Best Lock have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to make sure that products installed in fire-rated applications meet industry standards.

title: CPSC, ECR International Announce Recall to Repair of Gas Boilers
reason: The burners on these boilers could produce excess carbon monoxide (CO) in the flue, due to improper combustion, posing a risk of CO poisoning to consumers.
firm: ECR International, of Utica, N.Y.
distribution: Independent heating contractors sold and installed these boilers nationwide, from August 2001 through March 2002, for between $1,200 and $3,000.
hazards: The burners on these boilers could produce excess carbon monoxide (CO) in the flue, due to improper combustion, posing a risk of CO poisoning to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should contact ECR International immediately to arrange for a free repair. CPSC recommends that every home should have at least one CO alarm that meets the requirements of the most recent Underwriters Laboratories (UL) 2034 standard, International Approval Services 6-96 standard or the Canadian Standards Association 6.19-01 standard.
injuries: CPSC and ECR International have not received any reports of injuries or incidents relating to these boilers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Prestige Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Duckie Ring Rattle/Teethers
reason: The rattle may break, causing small beads to fall out, which presents a potential choking hazard to young children.
firm: Prestige Toy Corp., of New York, N.Y.
distribution: Retailers nationwide, including the Fred Meyer Co., The Carters Outlet Stores, Proffits and E.A.T. Gifts, sold the rattles, from March 2002 through April 2002, for about $7.
hazards: The rattle may break, causing small beads to fall out, which presents a potential choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the rattles away from children and return them to the company to receive a replacement toy or refund. Consumer should send the rattle to Prestige Toy Corp., 131 West 33rd Street. Room 606, New York, N.Y. Prestige will reimburse consumers for the cost of postage.
injuries: CPSC and Prestige have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Sherwood SCUBA LLC Announce Recall of Maximus Regulators
reason: The second stage orifices on these regulators can be cracked, bent or broken. This can result in a loss of breathing air underwater.
firm: Sherwood SCUBA LLC, of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Authorized Sherwood SCUBA distributors and dealers nationwide sold these regulators, from January 1998 through November 2000, for about $580.
hazards: The second stage orifices on these regulators can be cracked, bent or broken. This can result in a loss of breathing air underwater.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled regulators immediately, and contact their nearest authorized Sherwood retailer, for a free repair.
injuries: Sherwood SCUBA has received seven reports of broken second stage orifices on these regulators. Two of the regulators broke during dives underwater. No injuries were reported.

title: CPSC, Vermont Precision Woodworks Announce Recall of Cribs
reason: The slats on the cribs can loosen and detach from the drop side rail, creating a large opening between the slats, where a child's head or neck could become entrapped, resulting in serious injury or death.
firm: Vermont Precision Woodworks, of Morrisville, Vt.
distribution: Juvenile product and furniture stores sold the cribs nationwide, from January 2000 through March 2002, for between $500 and $800.
hazards: The slats on the cribs can loosen and detach from the drop side rail, creating a large opening between the slats, where a child's head or neck could become entrapped, resulting in serious injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled cribs until the repair has been performed. Vermont Precision Woodworks is providing consumers with replacement drop side rails.
injuries: Vermont Precision Woodworks has received 21 reports of slats detaching. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Specialized Bicycle Components Inc. Announce Recall of Bicycles
reason: The rear seatstays, the tube behind the seat that connects the rear axle to the rear shock, can break, possibly causing the rider to lose control and crash.
distribution: Authorized Specialized dealers nationwide sold these bicycles, from September 2001 through February 2002, for between $1,650 and $2,750.
hazards: The rear seatstays, the tube behind the seat that connects the rear axle to the rear shock, can break, possibly causing the rider to lose control and crash.
remedies: Consumers should stop riding these bicycles immediately, and return them to their local Specialized dealer for a new rear seatstay, which will be installed, at no charge.
injuries: Specialized Bicycles has received 39 reports of the seatstays on these bicycles breaking. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, InSTEP LLC Announce Recall of Trailer Bikes
reason: The bike's universal joint system can fail, causing a rider to lose control of the bike. This poses a risk of injury to either of the two riders.
distribution: Retail stores nationwide, including Toys "R" Us, The Sports Authority and One Step Ahead, sold the bikes, from February 2001 through May 2001, for between $80 and $110.
hazards: The bike's universal joint system can fail, causing a rider to lose control of the bike. This poses a risk of injury to either of the two riders.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these trailer bikes immediately and contact InSTEP for a free repair kit with instructions.
injuries: CPSC and InSTEP have received 10 reports of universal joint systems failing, including three reports of consumers who suffered contusions and abrasions.

title: CPSC, Coast Energy Management Announce Recall of Power Saving Devices
reason: The Power Planner is a device connected between motorized appliances and wall outlets that is intended to save electricity. These Power Planners have reversed polarity, posing a shock hazard to consumers.
firm: Coast Energy Management Inc., of Chandler, Ariz.
distribution: Home Depot, Costco, and Orchard Supply Hardware stores sold these Power Planners, from September 2000 through April 2002, for between $40 and $45.
hazards: The Power Planner is a device connected between motorized appliances and wall outlets that is intended to save electricity. These Power Planners have reversed polarity, posing a shock hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should unplug these devices immediately. Coast Energy Management is out of business, and a remedy is no longer available. Do not use this product. Please discard or destroy this product. Do not donate or resell.
injuries: Coast Energy Management has not received any reports of incidents or injuries involving these Power Planners. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Horizon Fitness Announce Recall of Treadmills
reason: A component of the electronic control panel can malfunction, causing the motor and walking belt to rapidly accelerate and the user can lose balance and fall.
firm: Horizon Fitness, of DeForest, Wis.
distribution: Sporting goods stores, including Total Fitness Solutions, Fitness Warehouse and Play It Again Sports sold these treadmills nationwide, from November 2000 through June 2001, for between $699 and $1099.
hazards: A component of the electronic control panel can malfunction, causing the motor and walking belt to rapidly accelerate and the user can lose balance and fall.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these treadmills immediately and contact Horizon Fitness to receive a repair kit and to set up an appointment to receive an in-home repair.
injuries: Horizon Fitness and CPSC have received 15 reports of consumers losing their balance and falling off of the treadmill. Injuries include cuts and abrasions.

title: CPSC, SC Johnson Announce Recall of Glade® Extra Outlet Scented Oil Air Fresheners
product: Glade® Extra Outlet Scented Oil Air Fresheners
reason: These Extra Outlet PlugIns® may have been misassembled during manufacture, which could pose a risk of fire.
firm: SC Johnson, of Racine, Wisc.
distribution: Grocery and retail stores nationwide sold the air fresheners, between January 2002 and April 2002, for between $4 and $5.
hazards: These Extra Outlet PlugIns® may have been misassembled during manufacture, which could pose a risk of fire.
remedies: Consumers should immediately unplug the air fresheners and contact SC Johnson for free, full value replacement coupons or a refund.
injuries: SC Johnson has received five reports of misassembly and no reports of injury or property damage.

title: CPSC, Hallmark Announce Recall of Harry Potter Key Chains
product: Harry Potter Magic Potion Bottle key chains
reason: The key chains can leak petroleum distillates, which can pose an ingestion hazard to children.
firm: Hallmark Cards Inc., of Kansas City, Mo.
distribution: Hallmark, Hallmark Card, Wal-Mart, grocery, drug, and gift stores nationwide sold the key chains, from October 2001 through November 2001, for about $5.
hazards: The key chains can leak petroleum distillates, which can pose an ingestion hazard to children.
remedies: Consumers should take the key chains away from children immediately and contact Hallmark for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Hallmark have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Estes Industries Announce Recall of Air Powered Rockets
product: GL-X200™ Estes Air™ Powered Rocket Systems
reason: The rockets' foam tips can break off, exposing sharp edges that can cause face lacerations or eye injuries to consumers. The rocket systems also have weak pump handles that can break during use, posing a risk of hand lacerations to consumers.
distribution: Department stores nationwide, including Wal-Mart, Toys R Us and Zany Brainy, as well as e-businesses, catalogers and hobby shops sold these rockets, from February 2001 through February 2002, for between $20 and $40.
hazards: The rockets' foam tips can break off, exposing sharp edges that can cause face lacerations or eye injuries to consumers. The rocket systems also have weak pump handles that can break during use, posing a risk of hand lacerations to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the air rockets immediately and contact Estes Industries for information on how to get a replacement rocket.
injuries: Estes and CPSC have received 16 reports of rocket tips breaking off. Six children were struck in the face by the rockets, including two children who suffered detached retinas and four children who suffered lacerations that required stitches or sutures. There were 68 reports of broken pump handles, including six hand lacerations.

title: CPSC, Brunswick Corp. Announce Another Expanded Recall of Mongoose and Roadmaster Mountain Bicycles
product: Mongoose and Roadmaster mountain bicycles with Ballistic 105 front suspension forks
reason: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control, fall and suffer serious injury.
firm: Brunswick Corp., of Lake Forest, Ill.
distribution: Discount department stores and toy stores nationwide sold the bicycles with these forks from, June 1998 through December 2000, for between $125 and $150. Additionally, consumers could have received a Ballistic model 105 fork as a replacement, when participating in one of the previous recalls.
hazards: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control, fall and suffer serious injury.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these bicycles and call the firm to obtain information on receiving a $65 refund for the bicycle fork. This applies to all owners of bicycles with Ballistic model 105 forks manufactured by Brunswick (except the Mongoose A40), even if they received a new Ballistic model 105 fork, as a result of participating in a previous recall.
injuries: There have been 34 reports of forks on these bicycles breaking, resulting in 31 riders, including children and teenagers, suffering serious head and bodily injuries, abrasions, bruises and chipped teeth.

title: CPSC, Ames True Temper Announce Recall of Wheelbarrows
reason: The plastic wheel assemblies on these wheelbarrows, manufactured by a predecessor company, can break when being inflated with high-pressure air hoses. This can result in plastic pieces exploding from the rims of the wheels, possibly hitting nearby consumers and causing lacerations and other injuries.
firm: Ames True Temper Inc., of Camp Hill, Pa.
distribution: Hardware stores and home centers nationwide sold the recalled wheelbarrows, from January 1993 through December 2000, for between $20 and $30.
hazards: The plastic wheel assemblies on these wheelbarrows, manufactured by a predecessor company, can break when being inflated with high-pressure air hoses. This can result in plastic pieces exploding from the rims of the wheels, possibly hitting nearby consumers and causing lacerations and other injuries.
remedies: Consumers should not inflate the tires on these wheelbarrows. Consumers should contact Ames True Temper to receive a free replacement steel wheel assembly.
injuries: Ames True Temper has received eight reports of plastic rims fracturing, seven of which involve lacerations to consumers' hands, face, chest or arms. Some of the lacerations were severe, and required numerous stitches. One report involved nasal and other facial bone fractures, three reports involved finger or knuckle fractures, and one report included torn wrist ligaments caused by the force of the pieces striking a consumer.

title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall for In-Home Repair of Infant Swings
reason: It is possible to misassemble the seats of these swings, so that they appear secure, but are not. If the seat of the swing is not properly attached, the seat and baby can flip forward.
distribution: Discount department and juvenile product stores nationwide sold these swings, from December 2001 through March 2002, for about $70.
hazards: It is possible to misassemble the seats of these swings, so that they appear secure, but are not. If the seat of the swing is not properly attached, the seat and baby can flip forward.
remedies: Consumers should stop using swings immediately and call Fisher-Price for help in inspecting the seat, to make sure the seat is properly attached. If the seat is not properly attached, a free replacement seat and revised instructions will be provided.
injuries: Fisher-Price has received seven reports of the seats of the swings flipping forward, including four reports of babies hitting their heads on the floor. Though bumps and red marks were reported, there have been no serious injuries.

title: CPSC, Country Home Products, Inc. Announce Recall for Repair of Cordless Electric Lawnmowers
reason: A wiring problem on the lawnmower's circuit board may cause some of the safety functions to become inoperable. The mower may continue to operate, after the Operator Presence Control Bar is released. The blade also may continue to spin for an extended period of time, after the mower has been shut off. Contact with a moving lawnmower blade can result in lacerations or serious injury to the hand or foot.
firm: Country Home Products, Inc., of Vergennes, Vt.
distribution: The recalled lawnmowers were sold nationwide, from January 2000 to October 2001, for about $350.
hazards: A wiring problem on the lawnmower's circuit board may cause some of the safety functions to become inoperable. The mower may continue to operate, after the Operator Presence Control Bar is released. The blade also may continue to spin for an extended period of time, after the mower has been shut off. Contact with a moving lawnmower blade can result in lacerations or serious injury to the hand or foot.
remedies: Consumers with a recalled lawn mower should immediately stop using the lawnmower. Country Home Products is sending all registered users of a Whisperlite® mower a repair kit. If you have not received a repair kit by May 1, 2002, please contact Country Home Products to request a free repair kit.
injuries: Country Home Products has received up to 300 reports of circuit board failures, with one incident resulting in a minor finger injury.

title: CPSC and Gas-Fired Products Inc. Announce Recall of Water Heaters
product: Seahorse® and "Bradford & White" Outdoor Gas-Powered Water Heaters
reason: Over time, the heat exchanger could become blocked, creating a potential ventilation and cracking problem, posing a fire hazard, if nearby combustibles ignite.
firm: Gas-Fired Products Inc., of Charlotte, N.C.
distribution: The water heaters were sold nationwide by retailers and also by public gas companies in North Carolina and South Carolina, between August 1992 and November 2000, for about $900.
hazards: Over time, the heat exchanger could become blocked, creating a potential ventilation and cracking problem, posing a fire hazard, if nearby combustibles ignite.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the water heaters immediately and contact the recall hotline to receive a free repair kit. Most consumers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
injuries: CPSC and Gas-Fired Products Inc have received reports of 2 incidents involving minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, DeWALT Industrial Tool Co. Announce Recall to Repair Circular Saws
reason: The spindle on the saw may slip, causing the blade to contact the lower guard, posing a hazard to the consumer, from an exposed blade.
firm: DeWALT Industrial Tool Co., Baltimore, Md.
distribution: Home centers and hardware stores nationwide sold the circular saws, from July 2001 through December 2001, for between $120 and $135.
hazards: The spindle on the saw may slip, causing the blade to contact the lower guard, posing a hazard to the consumer, from an exposed blade.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the circular saws immediately and return them to the nearest DeWALT service center, for a free repair.
injuries: DeWALT received one report of the blade slipping. A consumer received minor scratches to his hand after his spindle slipped.

title: CPSC, Crystal Mountain Water Cooler Corp. Announce Recall of Water Coolers
reason: The hot & cold water dispenser's heater band can short circuit, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
firm: Crystal Mountain Water Cooler Corp., of Alberta, Canada
distribution: Crystal Mountain and its distributors sold these water coolers in the U.S. and Canada, from May 1999 through July 2000, for about $300.
hazards: The hot & cold water dispenser's heater band can short circuit, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should turn off the hot tank power switch or simply unplug the units and contact Crystal Mountain to receive repair information. Consumers should have the serial number of their water cooler available at the time of the call.
injuries: Crystal Mountain Water Cooler Corp. has received about 20 reports of the water cooler's insulation smoking, or igniting the unit. Damages ranged from minor smoke and fire damage up to $200,000 in property damage.

title: CPSC, Wenzel Reminds Consumers about Recall of Propane Camping Lanterns
product: Ozark Trail or "Wenzel" propane-fueled camping lanterns
reason: An insufficient connection between the lantern and the propane cylinder can allow gas to escape and ignite unexpectedly, posing a potential fire and injury hazard to consumers. This hazard can occur during the lighting or normal use of the lantern.
firm: Wenzel Co., of St. Louis, Mo.
distribution: Wal-Mart sold the lanterns nationwide under the "Ozark Trail" label, from March 1999 through August 2001, for about $18. Sporting goods, camping equipment, and other retail stores nationwide sold these lanterns under the "Wenzel" brand, from January 1999 through August 2001, for between $18 and $28.
hazards: An insufficient connection between the lantern and the propane cylinder can allow gas to escape and ignite unexpectedly, posing a potential fire and injury hazard to consumers. This hazard can occur during the lighting or normal use of the lantern.
remedies: Consumers with Ozark Trail or Wenzel lanterns should stop using them immediately and detach the lantern from the propane cylinder. Consumers should return only the lanterns to the store where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: Wenzel has received 12 reports of propane gas escaping from these lanterns and igniting unexpectedly. Two consumers sustained burns to the arm and hand. One of the consumers also suffered burns to the eye.

title: CPSC, Intercon Merchandising Source Announce Recall of Mini Beach Chairs Given with "Time Out" Cosmetics at Sears
product: Time Out folding mini beach chairs
reason: The chairs can collapse, posing crush and amputation hazards to consumer's fingers and toes.
distribution: Sears stores nationwide distributed the mini beach chairs, with the purchase of $20 worth Time Out cosmetics, from June 2000 through August 2000.
hazards: The chairs can collapse, posing crush and amputation hazards to consumer's fingers and toes.
remedies: Consumer should stop using these mini beach chairs immediately and contact Intercon for a free repair.
injuries: CPSC and Intercon are aware of one incident, in which the tip of a 3-year old girl's finger was amputated, when the chair collapsed.

title: CPSC, Discovery Toys Announce Recall of Children's Toy
product: Up, Down & Around toddler maze toys
reason: The plastic tubes can break from the wooden base, releasing beads, posing a choking hazard to young children.
firm: Discovery Toys, of Livermore, Ca.
distribution: Discovery Toys' Educational Consultants sold the recalled toy nationwide, from July 2001 to January 2002.
hazards: The plastic tubes can break from the wooden base, releasing beads, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the toy immediately and contact Discovery Toys to receive a free replacement. Purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
injuries: Discovery Toys has received nine reports of the tubes breaking. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC and Federated Merchandising Group Announce Recall of Girl's Capri Pant and Shirt Set
product: Greendog® girl's capri pant and shirt set
reason: The buttons in the center of the embroidered flowers on the shirt can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Macy's, Burdines, The Bon Marche, Rich's, Lazarus and Goldsmith's sold the capri sets nationwide, between January 2002 and February 2002, for about $26.
hazards: The buttons in the center of the embroidered flowers on the shirt can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these sets immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or store credit.
injuries: No injuries or incidents have been reported. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: Cadet Manufacturing Co. Recall of In-Wall Electric Heaters
product: RM and ZM model Cadet in-wall electric heaters
reason: When an RM or ZM model heatbox (replacing a ZA or RA model heatbox) is inserted into a ZAC wall can and wired through a fitting in the top-left wall can knock-out (see the picture), the RM or ZM model has the potential for continuous heater operation, regardless of thermostat settings or room temperature. This can cause the heater to overheat and catch nearby combustibles on fire.
firm: Cadet Manufacturing Co., of Vancouver, Wash.
distribution: The RM and ZM model heaters were distributed mainly in California, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington.
hazards: When an RM or ZM model heatbox (replacing a ZA or RA model heatbox) is inserted into a ZAC wall can and wired through a fitting in the top-left wall can knock-out (see the picture), the RM or ZM model has the potential for continuous heater operation, regardless of thermostat settings or room temperature. This can cause the heater to overheat and catch nearby combustibles on fire.
remedies: If the heater is part of the recall, stop using it immediately by turning it off at the electrical panel board (circuit breaker or fuse box). Consumers should contact Cadet to schedule a free repair. In July 2001, Cadet began directly notifying affected consumers who participated in the October 1997 and February 2000 heater recalls about this RM and ZM program and began arranging service calls.

title: CPSC and Tristar Products Inc. Announce Recall of Steam Cleaner
reason: The internal hose connected to the trigger in the handle can detach, allowing hot water and/or steam to escape, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
firm: Tristar Products Inc., of Parsippany, N.J.
distribution: HSN LP (Home Shopping Network) sold the Steam Buggy Deluxe nationwide, from December 2001 through January 2002, for about $129.
hazards: The internal hose connected to the trigger in the handle can detach, allowing hot water and/or steam to escape, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the Steam Buggy Deluxe immediately and contact Tristar customer service for information on how to ship the recalled product and get a replacement or refund. Tristar will pay for all shipping charges to return the product. Consumers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
injuries: CPSC and Tristar Products have received reports of 305 incidents, 214 of which involved consumers receiving burns to hands, arms, feet, and body.

title: CPSC, Tough Traveler Ltd. Announce Recall of Child Backpack Carriers
reason: A child could fall from a carrier when the seat restraint strap is not doubled-back through the slider if the carrier's safety harness is not used. The seat restraint strap is located between the child's legs when the child is seated.
firm: Tough Traveler Ltd., of Schenectady, N.Y.
distribution: These carriers were sold through specialty baby products and outdoor products retail stores, and through the Tough Traveler web site and mail order 800 number from December 2000 through February 2002 for between $157 and $186. Only certain Kid Carrier™, Filly™ and Stallion™ carriers sold during this time are included in this recall.
hazards: A child could fall from a carrier when the seat restraint strap is not doubled-back through the slider if the carrier's safety harness is not used. The seat restraint strap is located between the child's legs when the child is seated.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these carriers immediately and contact Tough Traveler to receive instructions on doubling back the strap through the slider.
injuries: Tough Traveler has received one report of a strap slipping through the slider and the carrier's safety harness not being used. The child did not fall from the carrier. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Lifetime Products Inc. and Escalade Sports Announce Recall to Repair Portable Basketball Hoops
reason: The basketball hoops may have a sharp protruding bolt on the players' side of the pole, that can cause serious leg or body lacerations to consumers, when the bolt is exposed.
firm: Lifetime Products Inc., of Clearfield, Utah; Escalade Sports, of Evansville, Ind.
distribution: Sporting goods, department and toy stores, including Wal-Mart, Kmart, Target and Toys R Us nationwide sold the Lifetime basketball hoops, between January 1994 and July 2000, and the Escalade Sports basketball hoops, between March 1994 and December 2001, for between $80 and $500.
hazards: The basketball hoops may have a sharp protruding bolt on the players' side of the pole, that can cause serious leg or body lacerations to consumers, when the bolt is exposed.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the basketball hoops immediately and contact Lifetime Products or Escalade Sports to receive free cap nuts to cover the bolts. Consumers should call and get a cap nut, regardless of whether their bolt protrudes or not.
injuries: CPSC and Lifetime Products Inc. have received 27 reports of injuries and Escalade Sports has received one report of injury from the basketball hoop bolt. Injuries include scrapes, deep lacerations and bruises. Several consumers required stitches for their injuries. Players have been cut when they bump into the pole as they drive toward the basket.

title: CPSC, Invensys Climate Controls Announce Recall of TS11 Thermal Safety Control Valve
reason: The lower body, with 1/4", 3/8", 7/16" inlet/outlet diameter, may have a machining defect that can create a thin wall on the bottom of the casting. The cast area may break through partially or completely in a circular pattern when rapped, causing an external leak. The leaking gas may cause a fire.
firm: Invensys Climate Controls - OEM Products Group, of Long Beach Calif., a division of Invensys Control Systems
distribution: The Thermal Safety Control Valves are installed in commercial ovens, ranges, and warmer trays by OEM manufacturers and service organizations.
hazards: The lower body, with 1/4", 3/8", 7/16" inlet/outlet diameter, may have a machining defect that can create a thin wall on the bottom of the casting. The cast area may break through partially or completely in a circular pattern when rapped, causing an external leak. The leaking gas may cause a fire.
remedies: Consumers who have one of these valves should return to the point of purchase or to Invensys.
injuries: No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Childcraft Education Corp. Announce Recall of Changing Table with Steps
reason: When one of the front doors is open, a child's finger can become stuck inside spaces between parts of the hinges, causing finger crushing or pinching to occur while the door is closing.
firm: Childcraft Education Corp., of Lancaster, Pa.
distribution: Childcraft Education Corp. sold the recalled changing tables with steps to daycare centers and pre-schools, from January 1998 to May 2001, for about $700.
hazards: When one of the front doors is open, a child's finger can become stuck inside spaces between parts of the hinges, causing finger crushing or pinching to occur while the door is closing.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these changing tables immediately and contact Childcraft Education Corp. to receive a free repair kit. Purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.
injuries: Childcraft Education Corp. has received two reports of children having had their fingers caught inside the hinges. One child required stitches and the other needed surgery.

title: CPSC, The Toro Company Announce Recall of Riding Mowers
reason: The riding mower's exhaust system can ignite fuel vapors from spilled fuel if the engine backfires.
firm: The Toro Company, of Bloomington, Minn.
distribution: Toro dealers nationwide sold these riding mowers, between January 1998 and December 2001, for between $6,000 and $7,300.
hazards: The riding mower's exhaust system can ignite fuel vapors from spilled fuel if the engine backfires.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled mowers and contact Toro or their local Toro dealer to determine if their riding mower's model numbers and serial numbers are included in the recall. The model and serial number are located on a decal located on the right side of the operating console below the seat. If needed, the dealer will schedule a repair of the riding mower's exhaust system.
injuries: Toro has received 10 reports of fires caused when these mowers backfired and ignited nearby fuel vapors. One serious burn injury was reported. Property damage was limited to varying degrees of damage to the mowers.

title: CPSC, Exmark Manufacturing Announce Recall of Riding Mowers
reason: The riding mower's exhaust system can ignite fuel vapors from spilled fuel if the engine backfires.
firm: Exmark Manufacturing, of Beatrice, Neb.
distribution: Exmark dealers nationwide sold these riding mowers, between January 1998 and December 2001, for between $6,000 and $7,300.
hazards: The riding mower's exhaust system can ignite fuel vapors from spilled fuel if the engine backfires.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these recalled mowers and contact Exmark or their local Exmark dealer to determine if their riding mower's model numbers and serial numbers are included in the recall. The model and serial numbers are visible from the right side of the unit. They are located on a decal on the right side of the controls console. If needed, the dealer will schedule a repair of the riding mower's exhaust system.
injuries: Exmark has received 15 reports of fires caused when these mowers backfired and ignited nearby fuel vapors. At least one serious burn injury was reported, and two other users reported minor burns. Property damage has varied from minor damage to the machine itself to several thousand dollars damage to other mowing equipment stored nearby.

title: CPSC, Dixon Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Riding Lawn Mowers
